description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-11 by running the port against ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-crystalline-graphite.endf (MAT=30).

DEFECT: src/thermr/mf7.rs parse_elastic() reads the LTHR=1 coherent-elastic section correctly, but for each of the LT extra-temperature LIST records it keeps ONLY the temperature value and THROWS AWAY the S(E) table:

    for _ in 0..lt {
        let list = cur.read_list()?;
        extra_temperatures_k.push(list.head.c1);   // <-- S values discarded
    }

Consequently CoherentElastic (mf7.rs:33) stores a single s_of_e for the base temperature, and CoherentElastic::cross_section(&self, e_ev) (src/thermr/coherent.rs:29) takes NO temperature argument. There is no way to evaluate sigma_coh_el at any temperature other than the base one.

The struct doc is honest about this ('their S tables are not yet retained'), but src/thermr/mod.rs:17 lists coherent as '**done**', which overstates it.

WHY IT MATTERS (HTR-10 critical path): graphite is the HTR-10 moderator and coherent elastic is its DOMINANT thermal channel (measured via the port at 0.0253 eV: sigma_coh_el = 4.55 b vs sigma_inel = 0.49 b, so ~90% of thermal scattering). The graphite evaluation tabulates 10 temperatures: 296, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 1000, 1200, 1600, 2000 K. The IAEA HTR-10 B1-B4 benchmarks are at 20/120/250 C (293/393/523 K) and operation runs hotter. Using the 296 K Bragg structure factor at 523 K or 1000 K gets the Debye-Waller suppression wrong and therefore the thermal spectrum and k_eff wrong.

FIX: retain the per-temperature S(E) tables (the LIST records also carry an LI interpolation scheme between temperatures), and give CoherentElastic a temperature-aware cross_section(e_ev, temp_k) / bragg_reflections(e_ev, temp_k). Related but distinct from op-cjw.22 (which is about interpolating the INELASTIC S(alpha,beta) across temperature).

SIZE: small-to-medium. The record layout is already parsed; this is retaining data that is currently dropped, plus threading a temperature through two methods and their callers (src/acer/thermal.rs is the only in-tree consumer).

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content: FIXED 2026-08-11 (this session; unverified-by-human, not committed yet). parse_elastic now retains every LT extra-temperature S(E) LIST (shared Bragg-edge grid validated, LI codes captured): CoherentElastic is now {bragg_energies_ev, temperatures_k, s_tables, temp_interp}. coherent.rs evaluates cross_section(e_ev, temp_k)/bragg_reflections(e_ev, temp_k)/s_of_e_at(temp_k) with the shared policy: NJOY rdelas tolerance match (T/1000+5 K) -> LI-law interpolation between bracketing tabulated temps -> NjoyError::TemperatureOutOfRange (new variant) outside the range. acer thermal_from_mf7 writes ITCE/ITCX from s_of_e_at(temp_k). MEASURED (tests/thermal_graphite_coherent.rs, MAT 30, 0.0253 eV, b/atom): 296K 4.5514, 400K 4.3731, 500K 4.2049, 600K 4.0418, 700K 3.8849, 800K 3.7344, 1000K 3.4529, 1200K 3.1968, 1600K 2.7529, 2000K 2.3871 - strictly decreasing (Debye-Waller), 48% suppression 296->2000K. Interpolated 523.15K = 4.1672 in (4.0418,4.2049); 393.15K = 4.3849 in (4.3731,4.5514); 293.15K snaps to 296K within tolerance and reports it. NOTE also found+fixed: endf::interp::terp1 had ENDF laws 3 and 4 SWAPPED vs ENDF-102/upstream endf.f90 (needed because MT4 extras are LI=4 log-lin in T); reconr linearize midpoint arm + its test updated. 393 lib tests + 6/6 graphite V&V pass, release mode.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
VERIFIED FIXED 2026-08-13. The defect described above is gone; the bead had simply not been closed.

EVIDENCE, from the current source rather than from docs:
  grep 'extra_temperatures_k.push' src/thermr/mf7.rs  -> NO MATCHES. The discarding loop no longer exists.

  CoherentElastic (src/thermr/mf7.rs:59) now retains everything the fix called for:
      bragg_energies_ev : Vec<f64>        -- shared Bragg-edge grid
      temperatures_k    : Vec<f64>        -- ALL tabulated temperatures, ascending
      s_tables          : Vec<Vec<f64>>   -- s_tables[j][i] = S(E_i, T_j), one row per temperature
      temp_interp       : Vec<u32>        -- the ENDF LI temperature-interpolation codes

  CoherentElastic::cross_section (src/thermr/coherent.rs:116) is temperature-aware:
      pub fn cross_section(&self, e_ev: f64, temp_k: f64) -> Result<f64, NjoyError>

  And it does the right thing at the edges, per the module docs: match within the NJOY tolerance T/1000 + 5 K
  (upstream thermr.f90::rdelas); otherwise interpolate point-by-point with the evaluation's own LI law; otherwise
  NjoyError::TemperatureOutOfRange -- explicitly 'Never a silent nearest-temperature snap'. That is stronger than the
  fix this bead asked for, which only required retaining the tables.

  The consumer was threaded through too: src/acer/thermal.rs calls cross_section(e, temp_k, natom).

TESTS: cargo test --release -p njoy-outram-park-fork coherent -> 15 passed, 0 failed. The three that matter for this
bead specifically:
    thermr::coherent::tests::cross_section_decreases_with_temperature   (Debye-Waller suppression is real)
    thermr::coherent::tests::interpolated_cross_section_is_bracketed    (LI interpolation between tabulated T)
    thermr::coherent::tests::out_of_range_temperature_is_an_error       (no silent snap)

CONSEQUENCE FOR op-hc2o: blocker 2 of 5 is cleared. The HTR-10 benchmark temperatures (293/393/523 K) are now
serviceable against the 10 tabulated graphite temperatures (296-2000 K) by interpolation rather than by using the
296 K structure factor everywhere.

NOTE the bead's own claim that 'src/thermr/mod.rs:17 lists coherent as done, which overstates it' is no longer true
either -- it is now accurate.

Also worth re-checking before acting on it: op-cjw.22 (inelastic temperature interpolation) was filed P4 on the
assumption that target temps are tabulated exactly, and op-hc2o notes that assumption FAILS for HTR-10. Given the
elastic side now interpolates properly, the inelastic side is the remaining half of the same problem.

title: njoy THERMR DEFECT: coherent-elastic discards the extra-temperature S(E) tables — sigma_coh_el is only ever available at the base temperature

description:
Handoff for work an agent was STOPPED MID-TASK on, 2026-08-11. It never filed its own follow-up, so this records where it actually stopped.

WHAT LANDED (committed at 4feb6c84, compiles clean, workspace cargo check --all-targets = 0 errors):
- crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver: NuclearGraphiteMatrixA3 and NuclearGraphiteIG110 added to SolidMaterial, with solid_database/nuclear_graphite.rs implementing them. No todo!(). All the non-exhaustive match sites the new enum variants created were filled — that is the enum-over-trait-object design working as intended, forcing every dispatch site to be handled.
- crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/: mod.rs (41 lines) + zbs.rs (317 lines, UNTESTED — see the sibling bead).

WHAT DID NOT LAND. The maintainer directed that all four nested conduction scales live in crates/tampines. Only the bed scale exists. Still to build, and they NEST — each level effective property is the next level input, which is why they belong together:

1. TRISO PARTICLE CONDUCTION. The coated-particle stack: UO2 kernel, porous carbon buffer, IPyC, SiC, OPyC. Cited HTR-10 geometry from the IAEA benchmark: kernel radius 0.025 cm, UO2 density 10.4 g/cm3, 5.0 g heavy metal per pebble, 17 percent enriched. MAINTAINER APPROVED REUSING crates/boon-lay, which already has four-layer TRISO CSG geometry and per-layer temperature-dependent properties — take the GEOMETRY and conduction properties, NOT the release model, which op-jyyp.10 records as unvalidated (its verification test wraps the reference assertion in catch_unwind and discards it). There is currently no tampines -> boon-lay dependency edge; add it as a path dependency. Both crates are GPL-3.0 so there is no licence question.
2. PEBBLE CONDUCTION. 6.0 cm sphere, 5.0 cm fuelled zone, unfuelled graphite shell, matrix graphite 1.73 g/cc. The fuelled zone is a TRISO dispersion in graphite, so its effective conductivity comes from level 1 plus a packing model — do not treat it as homogeneous graphite without saying so.
3. CONJUGATE HEAT TRANSFER. Bed to helium via the Wakao particle-to-fluid Nusselt correlation already in TUAS (nusselt_number_correlations/input_structs.rs:152, already expressed on pebble diameter, the right form), and the solid path onward to the reflector. Check what conjugate-heat machinery exists before writing new.
4. GRAPHITE/MODERATOR FEEDBACK CHANNEL (op-jyyp.6). Its own reactivity channel, NOT lumped into fuel Doppler — the large graphite mass is what gives HTR-10 its long thermal time constant and self-limiting transient response.

TEST WITH ANALYTIC LIMITS, which are genuinely falsifiable: uniform properties must collapse a multilayer solution to the single-material result; zero radiation must recover the stagnant-gas-plus-solid limit; effective conductivity must lie between series and parallel bounds. Each level independently testable so a failure localises to a scale.

Per Wang et al. 2014 (catalogued proprietary) treating the double heterogeneity as homogeneous costs roughly +2800 pcm in k_eff; the thermal analogue is real too, so state the homogenisation assumption at each level in the doc comments.
title: tampines: the remaining three pebble-bed conduction scales (TRISO, pebble, CHT) plus the feedback channel

description:
Sets the fuel-to-coolant temperature difference and therefore the Doppler feedback the kinetics sees. Without it the sim cannot report a credible fuel temperature.

SCOPE: radial conduction through the pebble — fuelled inner zone containing the TRISO particles, then the unfuelled graphite shell — to the pebble surface, coupled to the bed via the Wakao particle-to-fluid Nusselt correlation that already exists in TUAS (input_structs.rs:152, already expressed on pebble diameter, which is the right form).

NOTE: GeN-Foam has a pebble routine that was deliberately NOT ported; the appbuilder crate says so explicitly. Consider whether porting it is cheaper than writing fresh.

Current fhr_sim_v2 pebble TH does NOT transfer here — it is a single lumped enthalpy control volume for a UO2 pebble with externally supplied heat transfer coefficient and area, defaulting to a constant-heat-capacity heuristic. It is UO2, not a graphite matrix.

Depends on graphite properties.
title: HTR-10: radial pebble conduction, fuel zone to pebble surface

description:
The always-emitted _INDEX.md giving the external agent a map of the whole workspace.

Deterministic markdown transform of each docs/api.md: keep the module/item headings and the fenced 'pub ...' signature lines plus each item's FIRST doc line; drop prose bodies, examples, status tables. rustdoc-md emits flat headings (a submodule gets the same heading level as its parent -- recorded in scripts/gen_api_docs.py's own docstring), so the module tree CANNOT be reconstructed from heading depth. Do not try; carry the module path from the '# Module `x`' headings instead.

MUST be reproducible byte-for-byte from the same inputs -- no timestamps, no HashMap iteration order, no absolute paths in the output.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
DESIGN CHANGED DURING BUILD, on measurement. The approved design was ONE _INDEX.md holding a condensed signature index of every crate. Built and measured 2026-08-14 on the real workspace, that file came to 535,580 bytes = ~134k estimated tokens -- 67% of the 200k budget spent before a single crate's real documentation was uploaded. Composition was evenly spread (headings 25%, signatures 44%, descriptions 29%), so no single trim rescued it.

Split into a three-tier ladder instead, all flat, nothing lost: _INDEX.md is now a ~3.4 KB roster of all 37 crates; <crate>.index.md (~7-105 KB each) carries the condensed index for one crate; <crate>.api.md is the full rustdoc. Uploading every .index.md reproduces the old single file exactly, so the content is identical -- it just became optional. A crate whose full api.md is in the core set gets no .index.md, since that would pay twice for one crate out of one budget.

title: agent-docs: condensed signature index over ALL crates
